title: Every, no, any and some 每一、无、若干和一些
description: A picture lesson introducing the compound pronouns of 'every', 'no', 'any' and 'some'. Twelve pictures (a-l) illustrate everyone/everybody, everything, everywhere, anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere, no one/nobody, nothing, nowhere, someone/somebody and somewhere. The written exercises rewrite sentences and answer questions using these compounds, and the grammar workbook drills filling blanks and completing dialogues.
answer_note: Listening and written exercises A-D are model answers (suggested). Workbook A (Choose and write in the best word) and B (Situations) are from the workbook answer key (source-key, img/key-112-117.jpg). Grammar I-III are from the grammar workbook answer key (source-key, pdf p.552-553).

lesson.text: Everyone is asleep. Everybody is asleep.
I looked for my pen everywhere.
Is there anyone at home? Is there anybody at home?
Is there anything in that box?
I couldn't find my pen anywhere.
There's no one at home. There's nobody at home.
Where did you go yesterday? Nowhere. I stayed at home.
There's someone in the garden. There's somebody in the garden.
My glasses must be somewhere! You're wearing them!

lesson.title: Listen and answer the questions
lesson.instruction: Listen to the recording and answer the questions for each picture (a-l).
lesson.translation: 听录音并回答每组图片（a-l）的问题。

questions.prompt: Picture a: Everyone is asleep.
questions.answer: Everyone is asleep. Everybody is asleep.

questions.prompt: Picture b: Everything is untidy.
Picture c: Looking for a pen.
questions.answer: I looked for my pen everywhere.

questions.prompt: Picture d: At the door.
questions.answer: Is there anyone at home? Is there anybody at home?

questions.prompt: Picture e: The box.
questions.answer: Is there anything in that box?

questions.prompt: Picture f: Lost pen.
questions.answer: I couldn't find my pen anywhere.

questions.prompt: Picture g: Looking through the window.
questions.answer: There's no one at home. There's nobody at home.

questions.prompt: Picture h: The empty box.
Picture i: Watching television.
questions.answer: Where did you go yesterday? Nowhere. I stayed at home.

questions.prompt: Picture j: In the garden.
questions.answer: There's someone in the garden. There's somebody in the garden.

questions.prompt: Picture k: Under the chair.
Picture l: The glasses.
questions.answer: My glasses must be somewhere! You're wearing them!

practice.title: Written exercise A
practice.instruction: Rewrite these sentences using any/no with -one, -body, -thing, -where. (One example is given.)
practice.translation: 用 any/no 加 -one、-body、-thing、-where 改写以下句子。（已给出一个例子。）
practice.context: Model answers rewriting with no-compounds. Item 0 is the printed example.

questions.prompt: Example: I didn't buy anything. I bought nothing.
I didn't do anything.
I didn't see anyone.
I didn't go anywhere.
I didn't meet anybody.

practice.title: Written exercise B
practice.instruction: Answer these questions using no one. (One example is given.)
practice.translation: 用 no one 回答以下问题。（已给出一个例子。）
practice.context: Model answers using the any/no one pattern. Item 0 is the printed example.

questions.prompt: Did you see anyone?
questions.answer: No, I didn't see anyone. I saw no one.

questions.prompt: Did you hear anything?
questions.answer: No, I didn't hear anything. I heard nothing.

questions.prompt: Did you speak to anyone?
questions.answer: No, I didn't speak to anyone. I spoke to no one.

questions.prompt: Did you go anywhere?
questions.answer: No, I didn't go anywhere. I went nowhere.

questions.prompt: Did you buy anything?
questions.answer: No, I didn't buy anything. I bought nothing.

questions.prompt: Did you write to anybody?
questions.answer: No, I didn't write to anybody. I wrote to nobody.

questions.prompt: Did you meet anyone?
questions.answer: No, I didn't meet anyone. I met no one.

practice.title: Written exercise C
practice.instruction: Rewrite these sentences. (One example is given.)
practice.translation: 改写以下句子。（已给出一个例子。）
practice.context: Model answers using Everyone's/Everybody's. Item 0 is the printed example.

questions.prompt: They're all watching television.
They're all looking out of the window.
questions.answer: Everyone's looking out of the window.

questions.prompt: They're all hurrying to work.
They're all eating.
They're all drinking lemonade.

practice.title: Written exercise D
practice.instruction: Answer these questions. (One example is given.)
practice.translation: 回答以下问题。（已给出一个例子。）
practice.context: Model answers using anything/nothing and something. Item 0 is the printed example.

questions.prompt: Have you got anything to wear? What about Penny?
questions.answer: No, I haven't got anything to wear. I've got nothing to wear. She's got something to wear.

questions.prompt: Have you got anything to eat? What about Sam?
questions.answer: No, I haven't got anything to eat. I've got nothing to eat. He's got something to eat.

questions.prompt: Have you got anything to do? What about the children?
questions.answer: No, I haven't got anything to do. I've got nothing to do. They've got something to do.

questions.prompt: Have you got anything to drink? What about Jane?
questions.answer: No, I haven't got anything to drink. I've got nothing to drink. She's got something to drink.

questions.prompt: Have you got anything to read? What about Alan?
questions.answer: No, I haven't got anything to read. I've got nothing to read. He's got something to read.

practice.title: Practice A: Choose and write in the best word
practice.instruction: Everyone, no one, anyone, someone, etc. Choose and write in the best word for you. 选择最恰当的词。
practice.translation: 从 everyone、no one、anyone、someone 等中选择最恰当的词填入。
practice.context: Workbook L116 A: 11 multiple-choice items; item 1 is the printed example (everywhere).

questions.prompt: I've looked ___ for my glasses. (a) nowhere (b) anywhere (c) everywhere
There is ___ in our garden. (a) somebody (b) anybody (c) everybody
There isn't ___ in the cupboard for lunch. (a) something (b) anything (c) everything
We've just moved into this street, so we don't know ___ yet. (a) everyone (b) anyone (c) no one
Listen. I want to tell you ___. (a) anything (b) nothing (c) something
We have invited ___ to the party, but no one has answered yet. (a) everybody (b) anybody (c) somebody
I'm sure there is a good job for you ___. You must find it! (a) everywhere (b) nowhere (c) somewhere
I looked in our class 10 minutes ago. There wasn't ___ there. (a) somebody (b) anybody (c) everybody
___ in your room is dirty! You must clean it. (a) Something (b) Anything (c) Everything
She can't go to the party because she's got ___ to wear. (a) nothing (b) anything (c) everything
I'm hungry. I'd like ___ to eat. (a) nothing (b) something (c) everything

practice.title: Practice B: Situations
practice.instruction: Read these situations. What do you say in each? 根据以下情景写出你应该说的话。
practice.translation: 根据以下情景写出你应该说的话。

questions.prompt: You are with friends and want a glass of lemonade. How do you ask politely?
questions.answer: May I have a glass of lemonade, please?

questions.prompt: A friend is looking through a dirty glass window. You want to know if he/she can see anything. How do you ask?

grammar.title: Grammar I: Fill in the blanks with compounds of 'every', 'no', 'any' or 'some'
grammar.instruction: 用 every, no, any 或 some 的复合词填空。
grammar.translation: 用 every, no, any 或 some 的复合词填空。
grammar.key_source: pdf p.552-553 (新概念英语语法练习1)
grammar.context: 16 numbered sentences (22 blanks). Items 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 each have two blanks; where the key accepts two equivalent forms (nobody/no one), both are kept as separate fields.

questions.prompt: There is ___ interesting in the newspaper today. You must read it!
Can ___ read French? (blank 1 of 2)
We've got ___ here in French. (blank 2 of 2)
but we can't understand ___ in French. (blank 3 of 3)
He went ___ yesterday. He stayed at home.
I know ___ here. (blank 1 of 2)
I know ___ here. (alternate: no one)
Is there ___ cheap in the shop? I haven't got much money.
Are you going ___ now? (blank 1 of 2)
Yes, I'm going ___ for lunch. (blank 2 of 2)
Mrs. Jones is very lazy. ___ in her house is dirty and untidy.
They are looking for you ___. (blank 1 of 2)
They've got ___ important to tell you. (blank 2 of 2)
He goes ___ by aeroplane. He thinks an aeroplane is the fastest.
___ helped me. (blank 1 of 2)
___ helped me. (alternate: No one)
These poor people have ___ to live. They have no home.
I can remember ___ about it. I've forgotten all about it.
There must be ___ in the room. I heard a noise.
Can you see ___ in the sky? Yes, some stars.
I'm very thirsty. I want to buy ___ to drink.
Have you seen Mike? Yes, I saw him in front of the library just now. He must be ___ in the library now.
